courses.title: Physical Education I-II
special_notes: Class of 2029 needs PE I OR II, not both - modeled as a diploma-rule special case, not a normal 'take both' sequence.
Swimming is a required, graded phase of the course.
At least one of the two required semesters must be taken in person.
courses.description: Offers opportunities for developing leadership, physical fitness, sportsmanship, and working/playing together, covering a wide range of team sports, aerobics, health-related fitness activities, recreational activities, outdoor pursuits, individual and dual sports, and aquatics. Athletic attire required. Swimming is a required, graded phase of the course; students provide their own swimsuits and towels. At least one of the two required semesters must be taken in person.

courses.title: Alternative PE - II (sports/activity-based)

prerequisites.note: IHSAA sport or FC-qualifying activity (cheer, WGI percussion/color guard, ISSMA show choir/marching band)

special_notes: ACTIVE ONLY for Class of 2027 & 2028 per department guide - explicitly sunsetting, similar pattern to Social Studies' Personal Financial Literacy course.
Requires 1 additional in-person PE credit (summer or school year) plus an Edmentum online academic component.
courses.description: For activities that qualify, including IHSAA-sanctioned athletics, IASP-sponsored cheerleading, WGI percussion and color guard, and ISSMA-based show choir and marching band. Provides opportunities to actively participate in four areas not covered in PE I. Requires 1 additional in-person PE credit plus a companion academic component through Edmentum during the semester the sport/activity is completed.

courses.title: Applied Physical Education I-II
special_notes: Determined by case conference committee, least restrictive environment
Class of 2029 needs PE I or II, not both - same rule as standard PE
courses.description: Offered as determined by the case conference committee in the least restrictive environment, covering a wide range of team sports, aerobics, health-related fitness activities, strength training, recreational activities, outdoor pursuits, individual and dual sports, and aquatics. Athletic attire required. Swimming is a required, graded phase of the course; students provide their own swimsuits and towels.

courses.title: Health and Wellness
courses.description: Focuses on developing a wellness lifestyle in which students learn to appreciate and take responsibility for their own health and that of their future family, developing decision-making skills and recognizing short/long-term health consequences of behaviors. Includes units on nutrition, emotional health, stress reduction, substance abuse, growth and development, human sexuality, lifestyle-caused diseases, and communicable diseases.

courses.title: Elective PE (Weight Training)
courses.description: Designed for the non-athlete interested in improving muscular strength and endurance through a rigorous weight training program, also focusing on cardiorespiratory endurance, agility, plyometric and speed training, flexibility, and core strength/stability. Students may also develop and implement their own weight training program based on professional organization guidelines.

courses.title: Elective PE (Advanced Weight Training)

prerequisites.note: IHSAA-sanctioned athlete who's completed PE, OR non-athlete with instructor approval

special_notes: Sport-specific weight track (A/B/C) recommended by staff
courses.description: Designed for student-athletes interested in increasing athletic development through a rigorous weight training/agility program including calisthenics, weight training, flexibility, agility, and endurance training, with daily participation and dress required. Also covers the basics of Exercise Science/Kinesiology including anatomy, physiology, nutrition, program design, and research article discussions.

courses.title: Elective PE (Basketball 101)
courses.description: Students immerse themselves in the sport of basketball, developing and refining skills while implementing and analyzing game strategies through on-court activities. In the classroom, students learn to take stats and analyze data by watching and studying college and NBA games, learning the ins and outs of coaching, refereeing, scorekeeping, and statistics.

courses.title: Elective PE (Coeducational Recreation Games)
courses.description: Designed for students who wish to be involved in daily physical activity beyond the freshman year, emphasizing lifetime leisure activities including ultimate Frisbee, Flashball, wall ball, goof ball, mat ball, and other sport variations.

courses.title: Elective PE (Lifetime Activities)
courses.description: Designed to improve fitness and activity levels, with students participating in sports and activities suitable for a lifetime such as badminton, tennis, pickleball, frisbee, corn hole, and volleyball, along with yoga, walking, strength/resistance training, and cardio routines. Students investigate topics like establishing a target heart rate, balancing diet and exercise, and creating a fitness workout.

courses.title: Elective PE (Lifeguard Training)
special_notes: American Red Cross certification possible with 80%+ scores
courses.description: Offers opportunities to learn lifeguard techniques, first aid training, and CPR. Students who pass all parts with 80%+ scores are certified by the American Red Cross. All candidates must successfully complete a pretest in week one (6 laps swimming, 2-minute treading water, retrieving a 10-pound brick from 10 feet in 100 seconds). Certification also requires model behavior.

courses.title: Elective PE (Swimming & Water Games)
courses.description: Focuses on students being physically active each day through various pool activities including swimming laps, treading water, diving, water polo, volleyball, water stations, water games, and water aerobics, developing skills and attitudes that promote lifelong fitness.

courses.title: Elective PE (Team Sports)
special_notes: Can only be taken once during a student's high school career
courses.description: Offers opportunities to participate in a variety of sports including basketball, flag football, lacrosse, soccer, team handball, and volleyball in a competitive environment, developing strategies, citizenship, leadership, and social skills. Can only be taken once during a student's high school career.

courses.title: Advanced Lifeguarding (Career Exploration Internship)
courses.description: Students put their lifeguard certification into practice, working as an actual lifeguard in FC's pool during swim classes and assisting the instructor in the classroom with CPR/First Aid training. Includes a career exploration component used to calculate the semester grade.

courses.title: Applied PE Assistant (Career Exploration Internship)

prerequisites.note: B average or better, successful completion of PE I, instructor approval

courses.description: For students interested in helping students with special needs. The student aids the teacher in day-to-day classroom activities including one-on-one assistance, equipment set up/take down, and assisting with instruction, plus getting in the pool on Mondays to assist students with special needs. Includes a career exploration component used to calculate the semester grade.

_department_wide_rules: Maximum 8 credits total can be earned across ALL combined Elective PE courses - this is a cap the progress tracker should enforce, not just display, per department guide.
Class of 2029 needs PE I OR PE II, not both, for standard and Applied PE - different from older classes who may need both.
_flags_for_owner_review: pe-alternative-2 (Alternative PE-II): department guide says 'Class of 27 & 28 only' but the CTD/eligibility documents don't explicitly confirm this sunset date independently - confirmed from FCHS's own document only. Low risk but noting the single-source nature.
